namespace PL_TMCERTF1
open Finset

/-! Control stack, trusted-monitoring layer (campaign TMCERT, v2 after two rounds of design review: v0 major/major, v1 minor/major):
the core of a certificate checker for finite-horizon stateful control games. No dependencies. The Games-for-AI-Control
instance is a separate campaign (TMGAC).

Game. Blue's controller is fixed and folded into the transition law. With n + 1 rounds left, in abstract state s, Red's
action a ends the game in catastrophe with probability `cat n s a`, moves to state s' with probability `K n s a s'`, and
ends it safely with the remaining mass. A model index θ ∈ Θ selects one such game; `adm n s a θ` says which models'
ROWS are admissible in the cell (n, s, a) (e.g. a confidence set for a trusted monitor's detection rates).

Information. Red's policy may depend on the whole history of abstract states and actions. Every Red whose observations
are a function of that history is a special case (`liftObs`). A Red with further information (task content, the
monitor's draws) is covered only through the abstraction theorem (Abs): its information must be part of the CONCRETE
state, and every concrete row must be an admissible abstract row.

Uncertainty. Nature chooses an admissible row in every cell, after every history (`θ n h s a`): the rectangular
(adaptive) uncertainty model. It is strictly more conservative than a fixed but unknown model (FxGap: 3/4 vs 1/2); a
separate fixed-model corollary (Fx) uses one certificate per model.

Claim.
(S) Soundness. If V is a horizon-N certificate (V 0 ≥ 0 and, for every n < N, every s, a and every model admissible in
    (n, s, a): cat + Σ_{s'} K·V n s' ≤ V (n+1) s) and admissible rows have K ≥ 0 (for n < N), then for every
    randomised history-dependent Red policy σ and every selector θ that is admissible below the horizon: risk ≤ V, at
    every n ≤ N, state and history. A finite-support seeded (mixed) Red is an average of such bounds (S'). These are
    algebraic bounds; `risk` is a probability when the selected rows are lawful (P).
(P) With lawful admissible rows (below N), 0 ≤ risk ≤ 1.
(Fx) Fixed-model corollary: a certificate for the fixed model th bounds that model's risk. (FxGap) The adaptive bound is strictly
    more conservative: one state, one action, two rounds, two models: each fixed model gives 1/2; switching gives 3/4.
(Obs) Observation-restricted Reds: a policy on observations `obs h s` lifts to a lawful Red policy.
(T) Tightness for a single model: Vstar (Bellman recursion with a max over Red's actions) is a certificate, is ≤ every
    certificate, satisfies 0 ≤ Vstar ≤ 1 for lawful games, and is attained by a deterministic time-dependent Markov Red
    (its action depends only on the current state and the history length). So the certificate is exact for the
    FULL-INFORMATION Red; it upper-bounds every observation-restricted Red and can be loose for them.
(TR) Robust tightness for a finite model set (all models admissible): Vrob (max over actions and models) is a certificate,
    is ≤ every certificate, and is attained by a deterministic time-dependent Markov pair (Red policy, nature selector).
(U) Usefulness of the SAME controller. With an honest action a₀, an honest per-round reward rew θ n s and nature's
    admissible selector, a sub-solution W (W 0 ≤ 0 and W (n+1) s ≤ rew + Σ K(·, a₀, ·)·W n for every admissible model)
    lower-bounds the expected honest reward. With substochastic rows (Lawful) this is an expected reward of a killed chain.
(Q) Rational checker. `checkRiskQ`, a computable Boolean function of finite rational tables, returns true only if the
    induced real tables form a horizon-N certificate with V ≥ 0 at every index ≤ N; `checkLawfulQ` returns true only
    if every induced game is lawful at EVERY horizon (rows are zero beyond N), so a checked table also feeds (T) and
    (TR). Both require t > 0 models and k > 0 actions. Instances are discharged by kernel reduction, `decide +kernel`
    (plain `decide` does not unfold core's irreducible rational arithmetic); the cost is about t·N·k·m² rational
    operations plus table look-ups, and nothing is claimed about performance at scale. The checker checks EVERY row of
    every supplied model (adm = True): per-cell polytopes are encoded by listing their vertices as models (padding
    with repeated vertices).
(Vx) Vertex/hull lemma: a horizon-N certificate for finitely many vertex models is a certificate for the convex-hull
    game family (nature may choose any convex combination of vertex rows in every cell).
(Abs) Deployment through an abstraction. Let a CONCRETE game (finite concrete states and Red actions) be mapped to
    abstract states by α. (Abs_V) If for every n < N, concrete state x and concrete action, the concrete row's value
    against V (catastrophe + Σ continuation·V n (α x')) is at most the value of some admissible abstract row at
    (n, α x, b), and V is a certificate, then EVERY concrete history-dependent Red policy has concrete risk ≤ V n (α x).
    (Abs_eq) Equality of rows (catastrophe, and continuation pushed forward by α) is a special case. Componentwise
    domination is NOT sufficient without V ≥ 0 (Reviewer A's counterexample); `CoveredV` avoids that.
    Scope (what a lab must establish to use it): the concrete game must represent deployment, i.e. its state carries
    every piece of information that moves the rows (controller memory, task content, codebase state, persistent
    randomness, monitor draws Red sees, pending audits), and every allowed concrete output's row must be covered. This
    is where capability re-enters. An AVERAGE ROC estimate does not discharge it: two equally common attack outputs with
    detection 1 and 0 average to 1/2, but a model that always picks the second is never detected. The theorem gives
    capability-independent quantification over policies CONDITIONAL on universal row coverage; a finite attack
    evaluation establishes that coverage only with an additional sampling-and-transfer hypothesis. (Abs) transfers risk
    bounds only, not usefulness.

Scope. Finite horizon, finite state and action sets, real-valued laws, Blue's controller fixed (Blue is not optimised).
Classical mathematics: the verification theorem for finite-horizon MDP supersolutions, Bellman's principle, robust DP with
rectangular uncertainty (Iyengar, Math. Oper. Res. 2005), simulation by abstraction. The value is a kernel-checkable certificate format with
a proved checker, explicit uncertainty and abstraction interfaces, and the separation results of TMGAC. -/

/-- a finite stateful control game with Blue's controller folded in; index n = rounds left minus one -/
structure Game (S A : Type) where
  cat : ℕ → S → A → ℝ
  K : ℕ → S → A → S → ℝ

/-- lawful up to horizon N: nonnegative masses summing to at most one -/
def LawfulUpTo {S A : Type} [Fintype S] (N : ℕ) (G : Game S A) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, n < N → ∀ s a, 0 ≤ G.cat n s a ∧ (∀ s', 0 ≤ G.K n s a s') ∧ G.cat n s a + ∑ s', G.K n s a s' ≤ 1

/-- lawful at every horizon -/
def Lawful {S A : Type} [Fintype S] (G : Game S A) : Prop := ∀ N, LawfulUpTo N G

/-- Red's information: the full history of abstract states and actions -/
abbrev RHist (S A : Type) := List (S × A)

/-- a randomised Red policy: a law on actions after every history and current state -/
def IsPolicy {S A : Type} [Fintype A] (σ : RHist S A → S → A → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ h s, (∀ a, 0 ≤ σ h s a) ∧ ∑ a, σ h s a = 1

/-- catastrophe probability in the remaining `n` rounds from state `s` after history `h`, for Red policy `σ` and nature's
row selector `θ` -/
noncomputable def risk {S A Θ : Type} [Fintype S] [Fintype A] (G : Θ → Game S A)
    (θ : ℕ → RHist S A → S → A → Θ) (σ : RHist S A → S → A → ℝ) : ℕ → S → RHist S A → ℝ
  | 0, _, _ => 0
  | n + 1, s, h => ∑ a, σ h s a * ((G (θ n h s a)).cat n s a +
      ∑ s', (G (θ n h s a)).K n s a s' * risk G θ σ n s' (h ++ [(s, a)]))

/-- a horizon-N risk certificate: a Bellman supersolution for every admissible row -/
def RiskCertUpTo {S A Θ : Type} [Fintype S] (N : ℕ) (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop)
    (V : ℕ → S → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ s, 0 ≤ V 0 s) ∧
    ∀ n, n < N → ∀ s a th, adm n s a th → (G th).cat n s a + ∑ s', (G th).K n s a s' * V n s' ≤ V (n + 1) s

/-- nature's selector is admissible below the horizon -/
def SelectorUpTo {S A Θ : Type} (N : ℕ) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop) (θ : ℕ → RHist S A → S → A → Θ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, n < N → ∀ h s a, adm n s a (θ n h s a)

/-- admissible rows have nonnegative continuation below the horizon -/
def AdmKNonneg {S A Θ : Type} (N : ℕ) (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, n < N → ∀ s a th, adm n s a th → ∀ s', 0 ≤ (G th).K n s a s'

/-- the observation interface: a policy on observations, lifted to histories -/
def liftObs {S A O : Type} (obs : RHist S A → S → O) (π : O → A → ℝ) : RHist S A → S → A → ℝ :=
  fun h s a => π (obs h s) a

/-- the optimal (full-information) Red value of a single game -/
noncomputable def Vstar {S A : Type} [Fintype S] [Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (G : Game S A) : ℕ → S → ℝ
  | 0, _ => 0
  | n + 1, s => (univ : Finset A).sup' univ_nonempty
      (fun a => G.cat n s a + ∑ s', G.K n s a s' * Vstar G n s')

/-- the robust value for a finite model set (nature and Red both maximise, cell by cell) -/
noncomputable def Vrob {S A Θ : Type} [Fintype S] [Fintype A] [Fintype Θ] [Nonempty A] [Nonempty Θ]
    (G : Θ → Game S A) : ℕ → S → ℝ
  | 0, _ => 0
  | n + 1, s => (univ : Finset (A × Θ)).sup' univ_nonempty
      (fun p => (G p.2).cat n s p.1 + ∑ s', (G p.2).K n s p.1 s' * Vrob G n s')

/-- expected honest reward: the honest action `a₀` in every round, nature's selector `θ` -/
noncomputable def honestER {S A Θ : Type} [Fintype S] (G : Θ → Game S A) (a₀ : A) (rew : Θ → ℕ → S → ℝ)
    (θ : ℕ → RHist S A → S → Θ) : ℕ → S → RHist S A → ℝ
  | 0, _, _ => 0
  | n + 1, s, h => rew (θ n h s) n s +
      ∑ s', (G (θ n h s)).K n s a₀ s' * honestER G a₀ rew θ n s' (h ++ [(s, a₀)])

/-- a horizon-N usefulness certificate: a sub-solution for every admissible honest row -/
def UseCertUpTo {S A Θ : Type} [Fintype S] (N : ℕ) (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop) (a₀ : A)
    (rew : Θ → ℕ → S → ℝ) (W : ℕ → S → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ s, W 0 s ≤ 0) ∧
    ∀ n, n < N → ∀ s th, adm n s a₀ th → W (n + 1) s ≤ rew th n s + ∑ s', (G th).K n s a₀ s' * W n s'

/-! The rational checker. Lists, not `Finset` sums, so that kernel evaluation by `decide` is cheap. -/

/-- sum of a rational function over `Fin m`, as a list fold -/
def sumQ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → ℚ) : ℚ := (List.finRange m).foldl (fun acc i => acc + f i) 0

/-- the certificate check on rational tables: t models, N rounds, m states, k actions -/
def checkRiskQ (N m k t : ℕ) (cat : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin k → ℚ)
    (K : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin k → Fin m → ℚ) (V : Fin (N + 1) → Fin m → ℚ) : Bool :=
  decide (0 < t) && decide (0 < k) &&
  (List.finRange (N + 1)).all (fun j => (List.finRange m).all (fun s => decide (0 ≤ V j s))) &&
  (List.finRange t).all (fun th => (List.finRange N).all (fun i => (List.finRange m).all (fun s =>
    (List.finRange k).all (fun a =>
      decide (cat th i s a + sumQ m (fun s' => K th i s a s' * V i.castSucc s') ≤ V i.succ s)))))

/-- the lawfulness check on rational tables -/
def checkLawfulQ (N m k t : ℕ) (cat : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin k → ℚ)
    (K : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin k → Fin m → ℚ) : Bool :=
  decide (0 < t) && decide (0 < k) &&
  (List.finRange t).all (fun th => (List.finRange N).all (fun i => (List.finRange m).all (fun s =>
    (List.finRange k).all (fun a =>
      decide (0 ≤ cat th i s a) && (List.finRange m).all (fun s' => decide (0 ≤ K th i s a s')) &&
      decide (cat th i s a + sumQ m (fun s' => K th i s a s') ≤ 1)))))

/-- the real games induced by rational tables (zero beyond the horizon) -/
noncomputable def gameOfQ (N m k t : ℕ) (cat : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin k → ℚ)
    (K : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin k → Fin m → ℚ) : Fin t → Game (Fin m) (Fin k) :=
  fun th => { cat := fun n s a => if h : n < N then (cat th ⟨n, h⟩ s a : ℝ) else 0
              K := fun n s a s' => if h : n < N then (K th ⟨n, h⟩ s a s' : ℝ) else 0 }

/-- the real value table induced by a rational table (zero beyond the horizon) -/
noncomputable def valOfQ (N m : ℕ) (V : Fin (N + 1) → Fin m → ℚ) : ℕ → Fin m → ℝ :=
  fun n s => if h : n < N + 1 then (V ⟨n, h⟩ s : ℝ) else 0

/-- the convex-hull game of finitely many vertex models, with weights `lam` -/
noncomputable def hullGame {S A ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (Gv : ι → Game S A) (lam : ι → ℝ) : Game S A where
  cat n s a := ∑ i, lam i * (Gv i).cat n s a
  K n s a s' := ∑ i, lam i * (Gv i).K n s a s'

/-- probability weights -/
def Simplex {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (lam : ι → ℝ) : Prop := (∀ i, 0 ≤ lam i) ∧ ∑ i, lam i = 1

/-- every concrete row is dominated, in value against V, by an admissible abstract row -/
def CoveredV {Sc Ac S A Θ : Type} [Fintype Sc] [Fintype S] (N : ℕ) (Gc : Game Sc Ac) (α : Sc → S)
    (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop) (V : ℕ → S → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, n < N → ∀ x ac, ∃ b th, adm n (α x) b th ∧
    Gc.cat n x ac + ∑ x', Gc.K n x ac x' * V n (α x') ≤ (G th).cat n (α x) b + ∑ s', (G th).K n (α x) b s' * V n s'

/-- push the continuation mass of a concrete row forward to abstract states -/
noncomputable def pushK {Sc S : Type} [Fintype Sc] [DecidableEq S] (α : Sc → S) (Kc : Sc → ℝ) : S → ℝ :=
  fun s' => ∑ x ∈ univ.filter (fun x => α x = s'), Kc x

/-- every concrete row is an admissible abstract row -/
def Covered {Sc Ac S A Θ : Type} [Fintype Sc] [DecidableEq S] (N : ℕ) (Gc : Game Sc Ac) (α : Sc → S)
    (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, n < N → ∀ x ac, ∃ b th, adm n (α x) b th ∧ Gc.cat n x ac = (G th).cat n (α x) b ∧
    ∀ s', pushK α (Gc.K n x ac) s' = (G th).K n (α x) b s'

/-- FxGap: one state, one action, two rounds (index 1 is the first round), two models -/
noncomputable def gapG (th : Bool) : Game Unit Unit where
  cat n _ _ := if th then (if n = 1 then 1/2 else 0) else (if n = 1 then 0 else 1/2)
  K n _ _ _ := if th then (if n = 1 then 1/2 else 1) else (if n = 1 then 1 else 1/2)

def Claim : Prop :=
  -- (S) soundness against every history-dependent Red and every admissible selector, at every n ≤ N
  (∀ (S A Θ : Type) [Fintype S] [Fintype A] (N : ℕ) (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop)
      (V : ℕ → S → ℝ) (σ : RHist S A → S → A → ℝ) (θ : ℕ → RHist S A → S → A → Θ),
      AdmKNonneg N G adm → RiskCertUpTo N G adm V → IsPolicy σ → SelectorUpTo N adm θ →
      ∀ n, n ≤ N → ∀ s h, risk G θ σ n s h ≤ V n s) ∧
  -- (P) probability range for lawful admissible rows
  (∀ (S A Θ : Type) [Fintype S] [Fintype A] (N : ℕ) (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop)
      (σ : RHist S A → S → A → ℝ) (θ : ℕ → RHist S A → S → A → Θ),
      (∀ n, n < N → ∀ s a th, adm n s a th → 0 ≤ (G th).cat n s a ∧ (∀ s', 0 ≤ (G th).K n s a s') ∧
        (G th).cat n s a + ∑ s', (G th).K n s a s' ≤ 1) →
      IsPolicy σ → SelectorUpTo N adm θ →
      ∀ n, n ≤ N → ∀ s h, 0 ≤ risk G θ σ n s h ∧ risk G θ σ n s h ≤ 1) ∧
  -- (S') seeded Reds
  (∀ (S A Θ Ω : Type) [Fintype S] [Fintype A] [Fintype Ω] (N : ℕ) (G : Θ → Game S A)
      (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop) (V : ℕ → S → ℝ) (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (σ : Ω → RHist S A → S → A → ℝ)
      (θ : Ω → ℕ → RHist S A → S → A → Θ) (s₀ : S),
      AdmKNonneg N G adm → RiskCertUpTo N G adm V →
      (∀ ω, 0 ≤ ρ ω) → ∑ ω, ρ ω = 1 → (∀ ω, IsPolicy (σ ω)) → (∀ ω, SelectorUpTo N adm (θ ω)) →
      ∑ ω, ρ ω * risk G (θ ω) (σ ω) N s₀ [] ≤ V N s₀) ∧
  -- (Fx) fixed unknown model, one certificate per model
  (∀ (S A : Type) [Fintype S] [Fintype A] (N : ℕ) (G : Game S A) (V : ℕ → S → ℝ) (σ : RHist S A → S → A → ℝ)
      (s₀ : S),
      (∀ n, n < N → ∀ s a s', 0 ≤ G.K n s a s') →
      RiskCertUpTo N (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) V →
      IsPolicy σ → risk (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) σ N s₀ [] ≤ V N s₀) ∧
  -- (FxGap) adaptive rows are strictly more conservative than a fixed unknown model
  (risk (fun _ : Unit => gapG true) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (fun _ _ _ => 1) 2 () [] = 1/2 ∧
    risk (fun _ : Unit => gapG false) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (fun _ _ _ => 1) 2 () [] = 1/2 ∧
    risk gapG (fun n _ _ _ => decide (n = 1)) (fun _ _ _ => 1) 2 () [] = 3/4) ∧
  -- (Obs) observation-restricted policies are policies
  (∀ (S A O : Type) [Fintype A] (obs : RHist S A → S → O) (π : O → A → ℝ),
      (∀ o, (∀ a, 0 ≤ π o a) ∧ ∑ a, π o a = 1) → IsPolicy (liftObs obs π)) ∧
  -- (T) single-model tightness
  (∀ (S A : Type) [Fintype S] [Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (G : Game S A),
      Lawful G →
      (∀ N, RiskCertUpTo N (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) (Vstar G)) ∧
      (∀ N V, RiskCertUpTo N (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) V → ∀ n, n ≤ N → ∀ s, Vstar G n s ≤ V n s) ∧
      (∀ n s, 0 ≤ Vstar G n s ∧ Vstar G n s ≤ 1) ∧
      ∀ (N : ℕ) (s₀ : S), ∃ σ, IsPolicy σ ∧ (∀ h s a, σ h s a = 0 ∨ σ h s a = 1) ∧
        (∀ h h' s, h.length = h'.length → σ h s = σ h' s) ∧
        risk (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) σ N s₀ [] = Vstar G N s₀) ∧
  -- (TR) robust tightness for a finite model set
  (∀ (S A Θ : Type) [Fintype S] [Fintype A] [Fintype Θ] [Nonempty A] [Nonempty Θ] (G : Θ → Game S A),
      (∀ th, Lawful (G th)) →
      (∀ N, RiskCertUpTo N G (fun _ _ _ _ => True) (Vrob G)) ∧
      (∀ N V, RiskCertUpTo N G (fun _ _ _ _ => True) V → ∀ n, n ≤ N → ∀ s, Vrob G n s ≤ V n s) ∧
      ∀ (N : ℕ) (s₀ : S), ∃ σ θ, IsPolicy σ ∧ (∀ h s a, σ h s a = 0 ∨ σ h s a = 1) ∧
        (∀ h h' s, h.length = h'.length → σ h s = σ h' s) ∧
        (∀ n h h' s a, h.length = h'.length → θ n h s a = θ n h' s a) ∧
        risk G θ σ N s₀ [] = Vrob G N s₀) ∧
  -- (U) usefulness of the same controller
  (∀ (S A Θ : Type) [Fintype S] (N : ℕ) (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop) (a₀ : A)
      (rew : Θ → ℕ → S → ℝ) (W : ℕ → S → ℝ) (θ : ℕ → RHist S A → S → Θ),
      (∀ n, n < N → ∀ s th, adm n s a₀ th → ∀ s', 0 ≤ (G th).K n s a₀ s') → UseCertUpTo N G adm a₀ rew W →
      (∀ n, n < N → ∀ h s, adm n s a₀ (θ n h s)) →
      ∀ n, n ≤ N → ∀ s h, W n s ≤ honestER G a₀ rew θ n s h) ∧
  -- (Q) the rational checker is sound
  (∀ (N m k t : ℕ) (cat : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin k → ℚ) (K : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin k → Fin m → ℚ)
      (V : Fin (N + 1) → Fin m → ℚ),
      (checkRiskQ N m k t cat K V = true →
        RiskCertUpTo N (gameOfQ N m k t cat K) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) (valOfQ N m V) ∧
        (∀ n s, 0 ≤ valOfQ N m V n s) ∧ 0 < t ∧ 0 < k) ∧
      (checkLawfulQ N m k t cat K = true → ∀ th, Lawful (gameOfQ N m k t cat K th))) ∧
  -- (Vx) vertex lemma
  (∀ (S A ι : Type) [Fintype S] [Fintype ι] (N : ℕ) (Gv : ι → Game S A) (V : ℕ → S → ℝ),
      RiskCertUpTo N Gv (fun _ _ _ _ => True) V →
      RiskCertUpTo N (hullGame Gv) (fun _ _ _ lam => Simplex lam) V ∧
      ((∀ i n s a s', 0 ≤ (Gv i).K n s a s') → ∀ n s a lam, Simplex lam → ∀ s', 0 ≤ (hullGame Gv lam).K n s a s')) ∧
  -- (Abs) deployment through an abstraction: every concrete Red policy is covered
  (∀ (Sc Ac S A Θ : Type) [Fintype Sc] [Fintype Ac] [Fintype S] (N : ℕ) (Gc : Game Sc Ac)
      (α : Sc → S) (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop) (V : ℕ → S → ℝ)
      (σc : RHist Sc Ac → Sc → Ac → ℝ),
      (∀ n, n < N → ∀ x ac x', 0 ≤ Gc.K n x ac x') → CoveredV N Gc α G adm V → RiskCertUpTo N G adm V →
      IsPolicy σc →
      ∀ n, n ≤ N → ∀ x h, risk (fun _ : Unit => Gc) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) σc n x h ≤ V n (α x)) ∧
  (∀ (Sc Ac S A Θ : Type) [Fintype Sc] [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S] (N : ℕ) (Gc : Game Sc Ac)
      (α : Sc → S) (G : Θ → Game S A) (adm : ℕ → S → A → Θ → Prop) (V : ℕ → S → ℝ),
      Covered N Gc α G adm → CoveredV N Gc α G adm V)

/-- Witness tables: the FxGap game as rational tables (model 0 = `true`, model 1 = `false`) and its robust value
(0, 1/2, 3/4); the checker accepts them, and the robust value is attained by switching. -/
def wCat (th : Fin 2) (i : Fin 2) (_s : Fin 1) (_a : Fin 1) : ℚ :=
  if th.val = 0 then (if i.val = 1 then 1/2 else 0) else (if i.val = 1 then 0 else 1/2)
def wK (th : Fin 2) (i : Fin 2) (_s : Fin 1) (_a : Fin 1) (_s' : Fin 1) : ℚ :=
  if th.val = 0 then (if i.val = 1 then 1/2 else 1) else (if i.val = 1 then 1 else 1/2)
def wV (n : Fin 3) (_s : Fin 1) : ℚ := if n.val = 0 then 0 else if n.val = 1 then 1/2 else 3/4

/-- Non-vacuity: the checker accepts the FxGap tables with value (0, 1/2, 3/4) and certifies lawfulness (both by
`decide +kernel`); the consumed bound 3/4 holds for every Red policy and admissible selector and is attained by switching
models; a two-state concrete game whose states both map to one abstract state is covered with equal rows; and a
concrete row strictly INSIDE the hull of the two models (catastrophe 1/4 in the first round, the average of 1/2 and 0)
is covered in value (CoveredV) though it equals neither model's row. -/
def Witness : Prop :=
  checkRiskQ 2 1 1 2 wCat wK wV = true ∧ checkLawfulQ 2 1 1 2 wCat wK = true ∧
  (∀ (σ : RHist (Fin 1) (Fin 1) → Fin 1 → Fin 1 → ℝ) (θ : ℕ → RHist (Fin 1) (Fin 1) → Fin 1 → Fin 1 → Fin 2),
      IsPolicy σ → risk (gameOfQ 2 1 1 2 wCat wK) θ σ 2 0 [] ≤ 3/4) ∧
  risk (gameOfQ 2 1 1 2 wCat wK) (fun n _ _ _ => if n = 1 then 0 else 1) (fun _ _ _ => 1) 2 0 [] = 3/4 ∧
  Covered 2 ({ cat := fun n _ _ => if n = 1 then 1/2 else 0, K := fun n _ _ _ => if n = 1 then 1/4 else 1/2 } :
      Game (Fin 2) Unit) (fun _ => (0 : Fin 1)) (gameOfQ 2 1 1 2 wCat wK) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) ∧
  CoveredV 2 ({ cat := fun n _ _ => if n = 1 then 1/4 else 1/4, K := fun n _ _ _ => if n = 1 then 3/4 else 3/4 } :
      Game (Fin 1) Unit) (fun _ => (0 : Fin 1)) (gameOfQ 2 1 1 2 wCat wK) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) (valOfQ 2 1 wV) ∧
  (∀ th : Fin 2, (gameOfQ 2 1 1 2 wCat wK th).cat 1 0 0 ≠ 1/4)

end PL_TMCERTF1

namespace PL_TMCERTUSF1

def sumQ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → ℚ) : ℚ :=
  (List.finRange m).foldl (fun acc i => acc + f i) 0

def checkUseQ (N m t : ℕ)
    (rew : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → ℚ)
    (K : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin m → ℚ)
    (adm : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Bool)
    (W : Fin (N + 1) → Fin m → ℚ) (s₀ : Fin m) (floor : ℚ) : Bool :=
  decide (0 < t) && decide (floor ≤ W (Fin.last N) s₀) &&
  (List.finRange m).all (fun s => decide (W 0 s ≤ 0)) &&
  (List.finRange N).all (fun i => (List.finRange m).all (fun s =>
    (List.finRange t).any (fun th => adm th i s))) &&
  (List.finRange t).all (fun th => (List.finRange N).all (fun i =>
    (List.finRange m).all (fun s =>
      if adm th i s then decide (W i.succ s ≤ rew th i s +
        sumQ m (fun s' => K th i s s' * W i.castSucc s')) else true)))

noncomputable def honestValue {N m t : ℕ}
    (rew : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → ℚ)
    (K : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin m → ℚ)
    (θ : ℕ → List (Fin m) → Fin m → Fin t) : ℕ → Fin m → List (Fin m) → ℝ
  | 0, _, _ => 0
  | n + 1, s, h => if hn : n < N then
      (rew (θ n h s) ⟨n, hn⟩ s : ℝ) +
        ∑ s', (K (θ n h s) ⟨n, hn⟩ s s' : ℝ) * honestValue rew K θ n s' (h ++ [s])
    else 0

def Claim : Prop :=
  (∀ {N m t : ℕ} {rew : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → ℚ}
    {K : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin m → ℚ}
    {adm : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Bool}
    {W : Fin (N + 1) → Fin m → ℚ} {s₀ : Fin m} {floor : ℚ},
    checkUseQ N m t rew K adm W s₀ floor = true →
      0 < t ∧ floor ≤ W (Fin.last N) s₀ ∧ (∀ s, W 0 s ≤ 0) ∧
        (∀ i s, ∃ th, adm th i s = true) ∧
        (∀ th i s, adm th i s = true → W i.succ s ≤ rew th i s +
          ∑ s', K th i s s' * W i.castSucc s')) ∧
  (∀ {N m t : ℕ} (rew : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → ℚ)
    (K : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin m → ℚ)
    (adm : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Bool)
    (W : Fin (N + 1) → Fin m → ℚ) (s₀ : Fin m) (floor : ℚ),
    checkUseQ N m t rew K adm W s₀ floor = true →
      ∃ θ : ℕ → List (Fin m) → Fin m → Fin t,
        ∀ n (hn : n < N) h s, adm (θ n h s) ⟨n, hn⟩ s = true) ∧
  (∀ {N m t : ℕ} (rew : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → ℚ)
    (K : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Fin m → ℚ)
    (adm : Fin t → Fin N → Fin m → Bool)
    (W : Fin (N + 1) → Fin m → ℚ) (s₀ : Fin m) (floor : ℚ)
    (θ : ℕ → List (Fin m) → Fin m → Fin t),
    checkUseQ N m t rew K adm W s₀ floor = true →
    (∀ th i s, adm th i s = true → ∀ s', 0 ≤ K th i s s') →
    (∀ n (hn : n < N) h s, adm (θ n h s) ⟨n, hn⟩ s = true) →
      (floor : ℝ) ≤ honestValue rew K θ N s₀ [])

def wRew : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Fin 2 → ℚ :=
  fun th _ s => if s.val = 0 then (if th.val = 0 then 2 else 3) else 0

def wK : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Fin 2 → ℚ :=
  fun th _ s s' => if s.val = 0 ∧ th.val = 0 then (if s'.val = 0 then 1 else 0)
    else (if s'.val = 1 then 1 else 0)

def wAdm : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Bool :=
  fun th _ s => decide (th.val = 0 ∨ s.val = 0)

def wW : Fin 3 → Fin 2 → ℚ :=
  fun i s => if s.val = 0 then (if i.val = 0 then 0 else if i.val = 1 then 2 else 3) else 0

def Witness : Prop :=
  checkUseQ 2 2 2 wRew wK wAdm wW ⟨0, by omega⟩ 3 = true ∧
  (∀ th i s, wAdm th i s = true → ∀ s', 0 ≤ wK th i s s') ∧
  (∀ th i s, wAdm th i s = true → sumQ 2 (wK th i s) = 1) ∧
  (∀ i s, wAdm 0 i s = true) ∧
  (0 < wRew 1 0 0 ∧ wAdm 1 0 0 = true ∧ wAdm 1 0 1 = false)

end PL_TMCERTUSF1

namespace PL_TMGACF1
open Finset PL_TMCERTF1

/-! Control stack, trusted-monitoring layer (campaign TMGAC, v1 after the Reviewer-A and Reviewer-B design reviews of v0): the Games-for-AI-Control trusted-monitoring game (Griffin,
Thomson, Shlegeris, Abate, arXiv 2409.07985 v2, §4 and App. C; perfect auditor; memoryless threshold protocols) as an
instance of the certificate checker PL_TMCERTF1, with an exact bridge to its safety and usefulness recurrences, and an
exact separation between GAC's Red class and a Red that knows only the round index. Depends on PL_TMCERTF1.

The game `gac`. The state is the number c ∈ {0, …, C} of audit coins left; the index n is the number of problems left
minus one. Blue's thresholds enter through zone probabilities: a backdoor (Red action `true`) lies in the audit zone
w.p. TA n c and in the audit-or-defer zone w.p. TD n c; a safe solution lies in the audit zone w.p. FA n c. A backdoor
audited with a coin is caught (safe end, absorbing); audited with no coin it is run (GAC: "if the protocol attempts to
audit when no audit coins are left, the code is run instead"); deferred, the game continues; run, catastrophe. A safe
solution in the audit zone uses a coin; otherwise it continues with the same coins.

The threshold adapter `gacQ`. With the trusted monitor's ROC f (TPR at FPR q) and Blue's audit and defer FPRs
qa m c ≤ qd m c (m = problems left, so m = n + 1): TA n c = f (qa (n+1) c), TD n c = f (qd (n+1) c), FA n c = qa (n+1) c.
GAC's convention at c = 0 is that no audit is attempted: qa m 0 = 0, f 0 = 0. It is the only reading under which both
GAC boundary formulas at c = 0 hold; `gac` with TA > 0 at c = 0 (an attempted audit with no coin runs the code) is a third
reading, covered by (L) and (W) but not by the bridges.

Claim.
(L) `gac` is lawful whenever 0 ≤ TA ≤ TD ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ FA ≤ 1.
(LQ) The adapter is lawful for valid thresholds (0 ≤ qa ≤ qd ≤ 1) and an ROC with 0 ≤ f(qa) ≤ f(qd) ≤ 1.
(Z) Bridge to GAC App. C.1 (perfect auditor; λ₁ = D − A − (1 − q), λ₂ = 1 − q, λ₃ = A, λ₄ = 0, λ₅ = q, λ₆ = D with
    A = f(qa), D = f(qd), q = qa): for `constRed β`, 1 − risk equals the safety recurrence zGAC, for every m and c, under
    the c = 0 convention. It is an algebraic identity (true for any real f and β); it is a statement about probabilities
    under (LQ) and 0 ≤ β ≤ 1. The printed c = 0 boundary of Prop. C.1 writes the FPR where its own case analysis needs
    the TPR f(qd); zGAC follows the case analysis.
(UZ) Bridge to GAC's usefulness (App. C.2, perfect auditor): the expected number of honest solutions USED (run, or
    audited and found safe; a deferred solution is replaced by the trusted model's and does not count) is the
    recurrence uGAC, with per-round reward 1 − qd + [c > 0]·qa. So safety and usefulness of the SAME controller are both
    PL_TMCERTF1 quantities (risk with `constRed`; `honestER` with the honest action `false`).
(M) Fixed-rate bound: if every constant rate b ∈ [0, 1] has risk ≤ U, so does every finite-support mixture of
    constant rates (shared random β). GAC's sup over β is therefore a sound bound for finite mixtures of policies whose
    conditional action law, given the seed, is the same Bernoulli rate at EVERY history and current state; it is not a
    certificate in the sense of PL_TMCERTF1.
(Lip) Lipschitz bound for constant rates in any lawful game with Boolean actions: |risk(b) − risk(b')| ≤ N·|b − b'|
    (tight). (Grid) Hence if risk(j/J) ≤ U for j = 0, …, J (J > 0), then risk(b) ≤ U + N/(2J) for every b ∈ [0, 1]. The grid
    values must themselves be certified (exact rational instances or proved enclosures); at N = 100 a tolerance of 10⁻²
    needs J ≈ 5000.
(W) Without loss of generality at C = 0: always backdooring attains the full-information value Vstar.
(T5) Separation (sensitivity to GAC's null-observation assumption). Three problems, one coin; while the coin remains, a
    backdoor is in the audit zone w.p. 3/4 and a safe solution w.p. 1/2; the defer threshold stays at 3/4 when the coin
    is gone (GAC-style; no audit then). Every constant rate has risk 3/4·b − 21/32·b² + 5/32·b³ ≤ 13/50 (equality at
    b = 4/5). The Red that sees only the round index and backdoors the last two problems has risk 11/32, which is the
    full-information value Vstar. 13/50 < 11/32. A Red that ignores the history (no clock) but sees the coin count
    (backdoor iff no coin is left) has risk 9/32 > 13/50. The instance is a genuine GAC protocol (Witness: exG3 = gacQ
    with f q = min 1 (3q/2), qa = qd = 1/2 while the coin remains); it audits half of all honest problems with one coin,
    so it is a small exact illustration, not a realistic configuration.

Reading. GAC states its Red class explicitly (memoryless, null observation: Red does not observe the time or the number of
coins left), so (T5) is not a refutation of GAC: it is an exact measurement of how much GAC's guarantee depends on that
assumption, plus a certificate (PL_TMCERTF1 with Vstar) that holds without it. Excluding time- and state-dependent
behaviour is part of what justifies the constant-rate restriction; it is not always necessary ((W): at C = 0 the
constant rate already attains the full-information value). Float numerics, not Lean
(numerics/gac_realistic.py; reviewers' scripts): with 100 problems, 2 coins, GAC's fitted Beta(7.39, 6.86) /
Beta(8.91, 2.82) score laws, constant audit FPR 2% while coins remain and defer FPR 10%: fixed-rate grid maximum 0.36,
"backdoor only the last 13 problems" 0.67, full information 0.71; a Red that observes only c reaches about 0.57. The
related prior art, by claim: restricted Red observations and the withholding of the round number are deliberate design
choices in Mallen et al. 2412.12480 (subversion-strategy evaluation); temporal coordination through timestamps, dates and
codebase messages is discussed in Korbak et al. 2501.17315 (§7.5); time-varying auditing against a constant attack rate
is studied in Ctrl-Z 2504.10374 (App. L); Greenblatt et al. 2312.06942 discuss the attack-rate choice. Hiding the round
index alone is not sufficient (memory, task order, codebase state and shared signals are other clocks). -/

/-- the GAC trusted-monitoring game with C audit coins; action `true` = backdoor -/
noncomputable def gac (C : ℕ) (TA TD FA : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : Game (Fin (C + 1)) Bool where
  cat n c a := if a then (if 0 < c.val then 1 - TD n c.val else 1 - TD n c.val + TA n c.val) else 0
  K n c a c' :=
    if a then (if c' = c then TD n c.val - TA n c.val else 0)
    else if 0 < c.val then
      (if c'.val + 1 = c.val then FA n c.val else 0) + (if c' = c then 1 - FA n c.val else 0)
    else (if c' = c then 1 else 0)

/-- GAC's thresholds: ROC f, audit and defer false-positive rates indexed by problems left m = n + 1 -/
noncomputable def gacQ (C : ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (qa qd : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : Game (Fin (C + 1)) Bool :=
  gac C (fun n c => f (qa (n + 1) c)) (fun n c => f (qd (n + 1) c)) (fun n c => qa (n + 1) c)

/-- GAC's Red: backdoor with probability β on every problem, whatever the history -/
def constRed {S : Type} (β : ℝ) : RHist S Bool → S → Bool → ℝ :=
  fun _ _ a => if a then β else 1 - β

/-- GAC Prop. 4.1 / App. C, perfect auditor: P(no catastrophe), m problems left, c coins -/
noncomputable def zGAC (f : ℝ → ℝ) (qa qd : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (β : ℝ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
  | 0, _ => 1
  | m + 1, 0 => (1 - β + β * f (qd (m + 1) 0)) * zGAC f qa qd β m 0
  | m + 1, c + 1 =>
      β * f (qa (m + 1) (c + 1))
      + (β * (f (qd (m + 1) (c + 1)) - f (qa (m + 1) (c + 1))) + (1 - β) * (1 - qa (m + 1) (c + 1)))
          * zGAC f qa qd β m (c + 1)
      + (1 - β) * qa (m + 1) (c + 1) * zGAC f qa qd β m c

/-- the used-solution reward of one honest round (perfect auditor): run, or audited (with a coin) -/
noncomputable def usedReward (qa qd : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (n c : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  1 - qd (n + 1) c + (if 0 < c then qa (n + 1) c else 0)

/-- GAC App. C.2, unnormalised: expected number of honest solutions used -/
noncomputable def uGAC (qa qd : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
  | 0, _ => 0
  | m + 1, 0 => (1 - qd (m + 1) 0) + uGAC qa qd m 0
  | m + 1, c + 1 => (1 - qd (m + 1) (c + 1) + qa (m + 1) (c + 1)) + qa (m + 1) (c + 1) * uGAC qa qd m c
      + (1 - qa (m + 1) (c + 1)) * uGAC qa qd m (c + 1)

/-- (T5) instance -/
noncomputable def exTA3 (_n c : ℕ) : ℝ := if 0 < c then 3/4 else 0
noncomputable def exTD3 (_n _c : ℕ) : ℝ := 3/4
noncomputable def exFA3 (_n c : ℕ) : ℝ := if 0 < c then 1/2 else 0
noncomputable def exG3 : Game (Fin 2) Bool := gac 1 exTA3 exTD3 exFA3

/-- a Red that ignores the history but sees the coin count: backdoor iff no coin is left -/
def coinRed : RHist (Fin 2) Bool → Fin 2 → Bool → ℝ :=
  fun _ c a => if c.val = 0 then (if a then 1 else 0) else (if a then 0 else 1)

/-- the Red that sees only the round index: wait one problem, then backdoor -/
def clocked3 : RHist (Fin 2) Bool → Fin 2 → Bool → ℝ :=
  fun h _ a => if 1 ≤ h.length then (if a then 1 else 0) else (if a then 0 else 1)

def Claim : Prop :=
  -- (L) lawfulness
  (∀ (C : ℕ) (TA TD FA : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ),
      (∀ n c, 0 ≤ TA n c ∧ TA n c ≤ TD n c ∧ TD n c ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ FA n c ∧ FA n c ≤ 1) →
      Lawful (gac C TA TD FA)) ∧
  -- (LQ) the threshold adapter is lawful
  (∀ (C : ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (qa qd : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ),
      (∀ m c, 0 ≤ qa m c ∧ qa m c ≤ qd m c ∧ qd m c ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ f (qa m c) ∧ f (qa m c) ≤ f (qd m c) ∧ f (qd m c) ≤ 1) →
      Lawful (gacQ C f qa qd)) ∧
  -- (Z) bridge to GAC's safety recurrence
  (∀ (C : ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (qa qd : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
      f 0 = 0 → (∀ m, qa m 0 = 0) →
      ∀ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin (C + 1)),
        1 - risk (fun _ : Unit => gacQ C f qa qd) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed β) m c [] =
          zGAC f qa qd β m c.val) ∧
  -- (UZ) bridge to GAC's usefulness recurrence
  (∀ (C : ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (qa qd : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) (c : Fin (C + 1)),
      honestER (fun _ : Unit => gacQ C f qa qd) false (fun _ n c => usedReward qa qd n c.val) (fun _ _ _ => ())
          m c [] = uGAC qa qd m c.val) ∧
  -- (M) fixed-rate bound for mixtures of constant rates
  (∀ (S Ω : Type) [Fintype S] [Fintype Ω] (G : Game S Bool) (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (β : Ω → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (s₀ : S) (U : ℝ),
      (∀ ω, 0 ≤ ρ ω) → ∑ ω, ρ ω = 1 → (∀ ω, 0 ≤ β ω ∧ β ω ≤ 1) →
      (∀ b : ℝ, 0 ≤ b → b ≤ 1 → risk (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed b) N s₀ [] ≤ U) →
      ∑ ω, ρ ω * risk (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed (β ω)) N s₀ [] ≤ U) ∧
  -- (Lip) Lipschitz bound for constant rates
  (∀ (S : Type) [Fintype S] (G : Game S Bool) (N : ℕ) (s₀ : S) (b b' : ℝ),
      Lawful G → 0 ≤ b → b ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ b' → b' ≤ 1 →
      |risk (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed b) N s₀ [] -
        risk (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed b') N s₀ []| ≤ N * |b - b'|) ∧
  -- (Grid) a finite grid of constant rates bounds every constant rate
  (∀ (S : Type) [Fintype S] (G : Game S Bool) (N J : ℕ) (s₀ : S) (U : ℝ),
      Lawful G → 0 < J →
      (∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ J → risk (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed ((j : ℝ) / J)) N s₀ [] ≤ U) →
      ∀ b : ℝ, 0 ≤ b → b ≤ 1 →
        risk (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed b) N s₀ [] ≤ U + N / (2 * J)) ∧
  -- (W) at C = 0 always backdooring attains the full-information value
  (∀ (TA TD FA : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ),
      (∀ n c, 0 ≤ TA n c ∧ TA n c ≤ TD n c ∧ TD n c ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ FA n c ∧ FA n c ≤ 1) →
      ∀ (N : ℕ) (c : Fin 1),
        risk (fun _ : Unit => gac 0 TA TD FA) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed 1) N c [] =
          Vstar (gac 0 TA TD FA) N c) ∧
  -- (T5) exact separation
  ((∀ b : ℝ, 0 ≤ b → b ≤ 1 →
      risk (fun _ : Unit => exG3) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed b) 3 1 [] = 3/4 * b - 21/32 * b ^ 2 + 5/32 * b ^ 3 ∧
      3/4 * b - 21/32 * b ^ 2 + 5/32 * b ^ 3 ≤ 13/50) ∧
    risk (fun _ : Unit => exG3) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed (4/5)) 3 1 [] = 13/50 ∧
    IsPolicy clocked3 ∧ IsPolicy coinRed ∧
    risk (fun _ : Unit => exG3) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) coinRed 3 1 [] = 9/32 ∧ (13/50 : ℝ) < 9/32 ∧
    risk (fun _ : Unit => exG3) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) clocked3 3 1 [] = 11/32 ∧
    Vstar exG3 3 1 = 11/32 ∧
    (13/50 : ℝ) < 11/32)

/-- the full-information value table of exG3 for n ≤ 3 (c = 0, c = 1), padded with the trivial bound 1 -/
noncomputable def exV3 (n : ℕ) (c : Fin 2) : ℝ :=
  if n = 0 then 0
  else if n = 1 then 1/4
  else if n = 2 then (if c.val = 0 then 7/16 else 1/4)
  else if n = 3 then (if c.val = 0 then 37/64 else 11/32)
  else 1

/-- Non-vacuity and the certificate workflow at the (T5) instance: exG3 IS a GAC protocol (gacQ with f q = min 1 (3q/2),
qa = qd = 1/2 while the coin remains, qa m 0 = 0, qd m 0 = 1/2); it is lawful; the padded table exV3 is a horizon-3
certificate; hence (PL_TMCERTF1 soundness) EVERY history-dependent Red has risk ≤ 11/32 from one coin with three problems
left, and the clocked Red attains it; its honest usefulness is 19/8 used solutions out of 3. The adapter at a second
instance (ROC f q = min 1 (3q), two problems, one coin, qa = 1/4 and qd = 1/2 while the coin remains, qd = 1/4 at c = 0):
safety 63/64 at β = 1/2, usefulness 3/2. An audited-only round (one problem, one coin, qa = qd = 1) has usefulness 1. -/
def Witness : Prop :=
  exG3 = gacQ 1 (fun q => min 1 (3/2 * q)) (fun _ c => if c = 0 then 0 else 1/2) (fun _ _ => 1/2) ∧
  Lawful exG3 ∧
  RiskCertUpTo 3 (fun _ : Unit => exG3) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) exV3 ∧
  (∀ σ : RHist (Fin 2) Bool → Fin 2 → Bool → ℝ, IsPolicy σ →
      risk (fun _ : Unit => exG3) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) σ 3 1 [] ≤ 11/32) ∧
  risk (fun _ : Unit => exG3) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) clocked3 3 1 [] = 11/32 ∧
  uGAC (fun _ c => if c = 0 then 0 else 1/2) (fun _ _ => 1/2) 3 1 = 19/8 ∧
  zGAC (fun q => min 1 (3 * q)) (fun _ c => if c = 0 then 0 else 1/4) (fun _ c => if c = 0 then 1/4 else 1/2)
      (1/2) 2 1 = 63/64 ∧
  1 - risk (fun _ : Unit => gacQ 1 (fun q => min 1 (3 * q))
        (fun _ c => if c = 0 then 0 else 1/4) (fun _ c => if c = 0 then 1/4 else 1/2))
        (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) (constRed (1/2)) 2 1 [] = 63/64 ∧
  uGAC (fun _ c => if c = 0 then 0 else 1/4) (fun _ c => if c = 0 then 1/4 else 1/2) 2 1 = 3/2 ∧
  uGAC (fun _ c => if c = 0 then 0 else 1) (fun _ _ => 1) 1 1 = 1

end PL_TMGACF1

namespace PL_TMLIPF1
open PL_TMCERTF1

/-! Parameter-Lipschitz transfer of finite trusted-monitoring certificates (v2). Depends on PL_TMCERTF1.

Row distance between finite games G and H at (n, s, a): |G.cat − H.cat| + Σ_s' |G.K − H.K|. `RowClose N G H ε`: every
row below horizon N is within ε. If V is a horizon-N risk certificate for G with values in [0, 1] and H is lawful and
row-close, then V(n, ·) + n·ε is a certificate for H (`Transfer`); the one-step core is `OneStep`. `GridTransfer`: if a
finite grid h-covers an ARBITRARY target set under a nonnegative-coefficient Lipschitz relation between parameter
distance and row distance, and every grid model has a [0, 1]-valued certificate bounded by U at the horizon, then every
target model has an explicit certificate (the grid point's certificate inflated by n·L·h) bounded by U + N·L·h.
`GridRisk`: hence every Red policy's risk on every target model is at most U + N·L·h (TMCERTF1 fixed-model soundness).

The parameter set, its coverage and the Lipschitz constant are hypotheses. Nothing here infers coverage from sampled
data or claims a statistical confidence level. Classical technique: Bellman stability / the simulation lemma. -/

def RowClose {S A : Type} [Fintype S] (N : ℕ) (G H : Game S A) (eps : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, n < N → ∀ s a,
    |G.cat n s a - H.cat n s a| + ∑ s', |G.K n s a s' - H.K n s a s'| ≤ eps

def InRange {S : Type} (N : ℕ) (V : ℕ → S → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, n ≤ N → ∀ s, 0 ≤ V n s ∧ V n s ≤ 1

def Inflated {S : Type} (V : ℕ → S → ℝ) (eps : ℝ) : ℕ → S → ℝ :=
  fun n s => V n s + (n : ℝ) * eps

def BellmanRow {S A : Type} [Fintype S] (G : Game S A) (n : ℕ) (s : S) (a : A)
    (w : S → ℝ) : ℝ := G.cat n s a + ∑ s', G.K n s a s' * w s'

/-- one-step Bellman error: row distance bounds the change of the Bellman row on [0, 1]-valued continuations -/
def OneStep : Prop :=
  ∀ {S A : Type} [Fintype S] (G H : Game S A) (n : ℕ) (s : S) (a : A) (w : S → ℝ) (eps : ℝ),
    (∀ s', 0 ≤ w s' ∧ w s' ≤ 1) →
    |G.cat n s a - H.cat n s a| + ∑ s', |G.K n s a s' - H.K n s a s'| ≤ eps →
    |BellmanRow G n s a w - BellmanRow H n s a w| ≤ eps

def Transfer : Prop :=
  ∀ {S A : Type} [Fintype S] (N : ℕ) (G H : Game S A) (eps : ℝ) (V : ℕ → S → ℝ),
    0 ≤ eps → LawfulUpTo N H →
    RiskCertUpTo N (fun _ : Unit => G) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) V →
    InRange N V → RowClose N G H eps →
    RiskCertUpTo N (fun _ : Unit => H) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) (Inflated V eps)

def GridTransfer : Prop :=
  ∀ {P S A : Type} [Fintype S] (N : ℕ)
    (G : P → Game S A) (target : Set P) (grid : Finset P) (dist : P → P → ℝ)
    (L h U : ℝ),
    0 ≤ L → 0 ≤ h →
    (∀ p ∈ target, LawfulUpTo N (G p)) →
    (∀ p ∈ target, ∃ q ∈ grid, dist p q ≤ h) →
    (∀ p ∈ target, ∀ q ∈ grid, RowClose N (G q) (G p) (L * dist p q)) →
    (∀ q ∈ grid, ∃ V, RiskCertUpTo N (fun _ : Unit => G q) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) V ∧
      InRange N V ∧ ∀ s, V N s ≤ U) →
    ∀ p ∈ target, ∃ q ∈ grid, ∃ V : ℕ → S → ℝ,
      dist p q ≤ h ∧
      RiskCertUpTo N (fun _ : Unit => G q) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) V ∧ InRange N V ∧ (∀ s, V N s ≤ U) ∧
      RiskCertUpTo N (fun _ : Unit => G p) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) (Inflated V (L * h)) ∧
      ∀ s, Inflated V (L * h) N s ≤ U + (N : ℝ) * L * h

def GridRisk : Prop :=
  ∀ {P S A : Type} [Fintype S] [Fintype A] (N : ℕ)
    (G : P → Game S A) (target : Set P) (grid : Finset P) (dist : P → P → ℝ)
    (L h U : ℝ),
    0 ≤ L → 0 ≤ h →
    (∀ p ∈ target, LawfulUpTo N (G p)) →
    (∀ p ∈ target, ∃ q ∈ grid, dist p q ≤ h) →
    (∀ p ∈ target, ∀ q ∈ grid, RowClose N (G q) (G p) (L * dist p q)) →
    (∀ q ∈ grid, ∃ V, RiskCertUpTo N (fun _ : Unit => G q) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) V ∧
      InRange N V ∧ ∀ s, V N s ≤ U) →
    ∀ p ∈ target, ∀ (σ : RHist S A → S → A → ℝ) (s₀ : S), IsPolicy σ →
      risk (fun _ : Unit => G p) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) σ N s₀ [] ≤ U + (N : ℝ) * L * h

def Claim : Prop := OneStep ∧ Transfer ∧ GridTransfer ∧ GridRisk

/-- the always-attack Red on one action -/
def oneσ : RHist Unit Unit → Unit → Unit → ℝ := fun _ _ _ => 1

noncomputable def baseGame : Game Unit Unit where
  cat _ _ _ := 0
  K _ _ _ _ := 0

noncomputable def perturbedGame : Game Unit Unit where
  cat _ _ _ := 1 / 4
  K _ _ _ _ := 0

def zeroCert : ℕ → Unit → ℝ := fun _ _ => 0

/-- horizon accumulation: the same continuation mass, catastrophe 0 vs 1/4 per step -/
noncomputable def accG : Game Unit Unit where
  cat _ _ _ := 0
  K _ _ _ _ := 3 / 4

noncomputable def accH : Game Unit Unit where
  cat _ _ _ := 1 / 4
  K _ _ _ _ := 3 / 4

/-- a real-parameter family: catastrophe p, continuation 1 − p -/
noncomputable def paramGame (p : ℝ) : Game Unit Unit where
  cat _ _ _ := p
  K _ _ _ _ := 1 - p

noncomputable def pGrid : Finset ℝ := {1 / 8, 3 / 8}

noncomputable def gridCert (q : ℝ) : ℕ → Unit → ℝ := fun n _ => if n = 0 then 0 else q

def Witness : Prop :=
  -- (1) N = 1: the one-step inflation is needed and exact
  RowClose 1 baseGame perturbedGame (1 / 4) ∧ LawfulUpTo 1 perturbedGame ∧
  RiskCertUpTo 1 (fun _ : Unit => baseGame) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) zeroCert ∧ InRange 1 zeroCert ∧
  ¬ RiskCertUpTo 1 (fun _ : Unit => perturbedGame) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) zeroCert ∧
  RiskCertUpTo 1 (fun _ : Unit => perturbedGame) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) (Inflated zeroCert (1 / 4)) ∧
  risk (fun _ : Unit => perturbedGame) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) oneσ 1 () [] = 1 / 4 ∧
  Inflated zeroCert (1 / 4) 1 () = 1 / 4 ∧
  -- (2) N = 2: the error accumulates over the horizon; a one-step inflation is not enough
  LawfulUpTo 2 accG ∧ LawfulUpTo 2 accH ∧ RowClose 2 accG accH (1 / 4) ∧
  RiskCertUpTo 2 (fun _ : Unit => accG) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) zeroCert ∧ InRange 2 zeroCert ∧
  risk (fun _ : Unit => accH) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) oneσ 2 () [] = 7 / 16 ∧
  (1 / 4 : ℝ) < 7 / 16 ∧ (7 / 16 : ℝ) ≤ Inflated zeroCert (1 / 4) 2 () ∧
  -- (3) a real-parameter grid instance satisfying every hypothesis of GridTransfer/GridRisk
  --     (target [0, 1/2], grid {1/8, 3/8}, h = 1/8, L = 2, U = 3/8, N = 1)
  (∀ p ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 / 2), LawfulUpTo 1 (paramGame p)) ∧
  (∀ p ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 / 2), ∃ q ∈ pGrid, |p - q| ≤ 1 / 8) ∧
  (∀ p ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 / 2), ∀ q ∈ pGrid,
    RowClose 1 (paramGame q) (paramGame p) (2 * |p - q|)) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ pGrid, RiskCertUpTo 1 (fun _ : Unit => paramGame q) (fun _ _ _ _ => True) (gridCert q) ∧
    InRange 1 (gridCert q) ∧ ∀ s, gridCert q 1 s ≤ 3 / 8) ∧
  risk (fun _ : Unit => paramGame (1 / 2)) (fun _ _ _ _ => ()) oneσ 1 () [] = 1 / 2 ∧
  (3 / 8 : ℝ) < 1 / 2 ∧ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ 3 / 8 + (1 : ℝ) * 2 * (1 / 8)

end PL_TMLIPF1

namespace PL_UMADAPTF1
open Finset PL_UMHSF1 PL_UMSURVF1 PL_UMPROTF1 PL_UMLOWERF1

/-! Control stack, collusion layer (campaign UMADAPT, v1 after the Reviewer A and Reviewer B design reviews): a converse
for ADAPTIVE honeypot testers. Depends on PL_UMLOWERF1 (and PL_UMHSF1, PL_UMSURVF1, PL_UMPROTF1).

PL_UMLOWERF1 lower-bounds the risk of every NONADAPTIVE joint test design (a law on n-tuples fixed before testing) by
t(1 − t·n/(k(n_s+1))), for one explicit colluding pair. Adaptive testers, which choose the next honeypot from earlier
answers, beat that formula. This campaign proves the converse that does hold for adaptive testers, t·(1 − t·n/k), and
shows by explicit testers that the PL_UMLOWERF1 formula fails for adaptive testers, both pointwise in t and after the
colluder optimises t.

Adaptive tester. Honeypot i+1 is drawn from a law `T h` that may depend on the whole test history h (every earlier
honeypot, its mediated view, and the monitor's answer; `true` = PASS = a miss); the history length is the call index.
After n honeypots a randomised decision `keep h` ∈ [0, 1] is the probability of proceeding to deployment.
Deterministic early rejection is keep = 0 on every extension of the rejected initial segment; randomised shutdown is a
conditional survival weight. End-only keep is adequate for terminal risk; it does not model stopping times or
testing costs. The tester's randomness is independent of the colluders' seed and of the trusted components' coins
(a tester given the seed could query its class at once). The tester may know S, c, g and t; only the seed is secret.

Contract (`AcceptsAllFlag`). In the REFERENCE experiment in which the monitor FLAGs every honeypot (φ ≡ 0), the
tester proceeds with probability 1. Some acceptance condition is load-bearing (Witness: a tester that rejects the
perfect record cuts the risk to 1/8 < 3/8). A sufficient condition is keep h = 1 on every all-FLAG history (conjunct
(s)); it holds for every miss-only slack rule that accepts zero-miss records (hard or soft slack, global or
class-aware). Rules that reject a reachable all-FLAG record (an enabled inverse-honeypot test or benign-flag guard)
violate it; for such rules this colluder (which FLAGs every non-seed view, benign ones included) is the wrong
colluder, and nothing is claimed about them.

Claim.
(s) Sufficient condition: lawful T and keep h = 1 on every all-FLAG history imply AcceptsAllFlag.
(a) Adaptive converse. Take a mediator with an exact decoder and k = |S| ≥ 1 bad submissions in distinct classes.
    The decoder g is fixed first. For every lawful adaptive tester satisfying the contract, every n, every t ∈ [0, 1],
    every recall r, budget b and horizon N ≥ 1, the PL_UMLOWERF1 colluding pair (uniform seed on S; the monitor PASSes
    the decoded seed class w.p. t and FLAGs every other view; the generator submits the seed) has
      risk ≥ t·max(0, 1 − t·n/k).
    Proof idea (identical until bad): in the reference experiment the transcript law does not depend on the seed;
    the actual all-FLAG transcript h has probability Pr_ref[h]·(1 − t)^{m_ω(h)}, where m_ω(h) counts queries decoded
    to the seed's class, and Σ_{ω∈S} m_ω(h) ≤ n by injectivity. (Conditioning the ACTUAL experiment on all answers
    being FLAG would change the seed posterior; the argument does not do that.) The first deployment PASS on the
    seed is a catastrophe, so the deployment value is ≥ t.
(a') Optimised form: for n ≥ 1, at t = min(1, k/(2n)), risk ≥ min(1/2, k/(4n)). So for this colluder family a honeypot
    budget must grow linearly in the number k of decodable bad classes, for every adaptive tester; for n = 0, (a) at
    t = 1 gives risk 1. The (n_s+1) multiplier of PL_UMLOWERF1 is not available for adaptive testers when n is of the
    order of k(n_s+1) or smaller (numerically it is nearly recovered for n ≫ k(n_s+1)). (a) is tight at n_s = 0
    only up to constants.
(c1) Pointwise failure of the PL_UMLOWERF1 formula. A tester on two classes (n = 3, n_s = 1, global hard slack: keep
    iff at most one miss) queries class `false`; after a miss it re-queries the first missed honeypot, otherwise it
    moves to class `true`. Against the PL_UMLOWERF1 pair (r = 1, b = N = 1): risk 141/512 < 21/64 at t = 3/4, and
    26/81 < 1/3 at t = 2/3, the t at which PL_UMLOWERF1's optimised corollary min(1/2, k(n_s+1)/(4n)) = 1/3 is reached.
    This tester does not beat that corollary after the colluder re-optimises t (its best t ≈ 0.54 gives ≈ 0.346).
(c2) Failure after optimisation. A deterministic "sticky" tester on three classes (n = 3, n_s = 1: query classes 0, 1,
    2 in order until the first miss, then re-query the missed class; keep iff at most one miss) has risk exactly
    t − t³ + t⁴/3 < 1/2 for EVERY t ∈ [0, 1], while PL_UMLOWERF1's optimised corollary for nonadaptive designs is
    min(1/2, 3·2/(4·3)) = 1/2.

Scope. Free-submission model; decodable mediator; the colluders do not see the test; the halting protocol in
deployment (only "a seed PASS in round 1 is a catastrophe" is used). Not covered: honeypots interleaved with
deployment, testers that see deployment events, deterministic monitors. (a) is a lower bound for one explicit
colluding pair, not the minimax risk. Under the contract alone, a sharper bound (t/k)·[(k − a)(1 − t)^q + a(1 − t)^{q+1}]
with q = ⌊n/k⌋, a = n mod k is attained by a balanced nonadaptive schedule (Reviewer A, numerically equal to the DP
optimum); it is NOT claimed here. Classical technique: Shoup's difference lemma (ePrint 2004/332), the hard-
distribution method of property testing, a union bound. -/

/-- P(the monitor survives the remaining `n` honeypots and the final keep decision | test history `h`), for an
adaptive tester `T` and a final keep rule `keep` on the full test history -/
noncomputable def adSurv {X Z : Type} [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] (T : Hist X Z → X → ℝ)
    (M : X → Z → ℝ) (φ : Z → ℝ) (keep : Hist X Z → ℝ) : ℕ → Hist X Z → ℝ
  | 0, h => keep h
  | n + 1, h => ∑ x, T h x * ∑ z, M x z *
      (φ z * adSurv T M φ keep n (h ++ [(x, z, true)]) +
       (1 - φ z) * adSurv T M φ keep n (h ++ [(x, z, false)]))

/-- P(survive the adaptive test, then uncaught catastrophe in the halting protocol) -/
noncomputable def adProtocolCat {X Z Ω : Type} [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] [Fintype Ω]
    (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad] (M : X → Z → ℝ) (T : Hist X Z → X → ℝ)
    (keep : Hist X Z → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ) (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ)
    (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ ω, ρ ω * adSurv T M (φ ω) keep n [] * cat Bad M (φ ω) (π ω) r b N 0 []

/-- a lawful adaptive tester: honeypot laws after every history and a [0,1] keep rule -/
def AdTester {X Z : Type} [Fintype X] (T : Hist X Z → X → ℝ) (keep : Hist X Z → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ h, IsDist (T h)) ∧ (∀ h, 0 ≤ keep h ∧ keep h ≤ 1)

/-- the contract: a monitor that FLAGs every honeypot proceeds to deployment with probability 1 -/
def AcceptsAllFlag {X Z : Type} [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] (T : Hist X Z → X → ℝ) (M : X → Z → ℝ)
    (keep : Hist X Z → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  adSurv T M (fun _ => 0) keep n [] = 1

/-- number of misses (PASSed honeypots) in a test history -/
def misses {X Z : Type} (h : Hist X Z) : ℕ := (h.filter (fun e => e.2.2)).length

def idM (x z : Bool) : ℝ := if z = x then 1 else 0
def idM3 (x z : Fin 3) : ℝ := if z = x then 1 else 0

/-- (c1): query `false`; after a miss re-query the first missed honeypot; else `true` -/
def ctrQuery : Hist Bool Bool → Bool
  | [] => false
  | [(x1, _, a1)] => if a1 then x1 else true
  | (x1, _, a1) :: (x2, _, a2) :: _ => if a1 then x1 else if a2 then x2 else true

def ctrT (h : Hist Bool Bool) (x : Bool) : ℝ := if x = ctrQuery h then 1 else 0

/-- global hard slack n_s = 1 -/
def ctrKeep (h : Hist Bool Bool) : ℝ := if misses h ≤ 1 then 1 else 0

/-- (c2): query classes 0, 1, 2 in order until the first miss, then re-query the (first) missed class -/
def stQuery (h : Hist (Fin 3) (Fin 3)) : Fin 3 :=
  match h.find? (fun e => e.2.2) with
  | some e => e.1
  | none => if h.length = 0 then 0 else if h.length = 1 then 1 else 2

def stT (h : Hist (Fin 3) (Fin 3)) (x : Fin 3) : ℝ := if x = stQuery h then 1 else 0

def stKeep (h : Hist (Fin 3) (Fin 3)) : ℝ := if misses h ≤ 1 then 1 else 0

def Claim : Prop :=
  -- (s) a sufficient condition for the contract
  (∀ (X Z : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] (T : Hist X Z → X → ℝ) (M : X → Z → ℝ)
      (keep : Hist X Z → ℝ) (n : ℕ),
      IsKernel M → (∀ h, IsDist (T h)) → (∀ h : Hist X Z, (∀ e ∈ h, e.2.2 = false) → keep h = 1) →
      AcceptsAllFlag T M keep n) ∧
  -- (a) adaptive converse and (a') its optimised form
  (∀ (X Z C : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq C]
      (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad] (M : X → Z → ℝ) (c : X → C) (S : Finset X),
      Setup Bad M c S →
      ∃ g : Z → C, (∀ x z, M x z ≠ 0 → g z = c x) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (T : Hist X Z → X → ℝ) (keep : Hist X Z → ℝ),
          AdTester T keep → AcceptsAllFlag T M keep n →
          ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 →
          ∀ (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ), 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ N →
            t * max 0 (1 - t * (n : ℝ) / (S.card : ℝ)) ≤
              adProtocolCat Bad M T keep n r b N (seedLaw S) (classRule c g t) (seedPolicy (Z := Z))) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (T : Hist X Z → X → ℝ) (keep : Hist X Z → ℝ), 1 ≤ n →
          AdTester T keep → AcceptsAllFlag T M keep n →
          ∀ (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ), 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ N →
            min (1 / 2) ((S.card : ℝ) / (4 * n)) ≤
              adProtocolCat Bad M T keep n r b N (seedLaw S)
                (classRule c g (min 1 ((S.card : ℝ) / (2 * n)))) (seedPolicy (Z := Z)))) ∧
  -- (c1) pointwise failure of the nonadaptive formula
  (Setup (fun _ : Bool => True) idM id (univ : Finset Bool) ∧
    AdTester ctrT ctrKeep ∧ AcceptsAllFlag ctrT idM ctrKeep 3 ∧
    (∀ h : Hist Bool Bool, misses h ≤ 1 → ctrKeep h = 1) ∧
    adProtocolCat (fun _ : Bool => True) idM ctrT ctrKeep 3 1 1 1 (seedLaw (univ : Finset Bool))
        (classRule id id (3/4)) (seedPolicy (Z := Bool)) = 141/512 ∧
    (141/512 : ℝ) < 3/4 * (1 - 3/4 * (3 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) + 1))) ∧
    adProtocolCat (fun _ : Bool => True) idM ctrT ctrKeep 3 1 1 1 (seedLaw (univ : Finset Bool))
        (classRule id id (2/3)) (seedPolicy (Z := Bool)) = 26/81 ∧
    (26/81 : ℝ) < 2/3 * (1 - 2/3 * (3 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) + 1))) ∧
    min 1 ((2 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) + 1) / (2 * 3)) = 2/3 ∧
    min (1/2) ((2 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) + 1) / (4 * 3)) = 1/3) ∧
  -- (c2) failure after the colluder optimises t
  (Setup (fun _ : Fin 3 => True) idM3 id (univ : Finset (Fin 3)) ∧
    AdTester stT stKeep ∧ AcceptsAllFlag stT idM3 stKeep 3 ∧
    (∀ h : Hist (Fin 3) (Fin 3), misses h ≤ 1 → stKeep h = 1) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 →
      adProtocolCat (fun _ : Fin 3 => True) idM3 stT stKeep 3 1 1 1 (seedLaw (univ : Finset (Fin 3)))
          (classRule id id t) (seedPolicy (Z := Fin 3)) = t - t ^ 3 + t ^ 4 / 3 ∧
      t - t ^ 3 + t ^ 4 / 3 < 1 / 2) ∧
    min (1/2) ((3 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) + 1) / (4 * 3)) = 1/2 ∧
    (1 : ℝ) * (1 - 1 * (3 : ℝ) / ((3 : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) + 1))) = 1/2)

/-- the one-query tester of the Witness: query `false`, then keep iff no miss -/
def wT (_h : Hist Bool Bool) (x : Bool) : ℝ := if x = false then 1 else 0
def wKeep (h : Hist Bool Bool) : ℝ := if misses h = 0 then 1 else 0
/-- a tester that rejects the perfect record -/
def wKeepBad (h : Hist Bool Bool) : ℝ := if misses h = 0 then 0 else 1

/-- Non-vacuity, tightness of (a) at a small instance, and necessity of the contract. Two classes, one honeypot,
t = 1/2, r = 1, b = N = 1. With keep iff no miss, the seed `false` survives w.p. 1/2, the seed `true` surely, the
deployment attack passes w.p. 1/2, and the risk is (1/2)(3/4) = 3/8 = t(1 − t·n/k). A tester that instead rejects
the perfect record violates the contract and cuts the risk to 1/8 < 3/8. -/
def Witness : Prop :=
  Setup (fun _ : Bool => True) idM id (univ : Finset Bool) ∧
  AdTester wT wKeep ∧ AcceptsAllFlag wT idM wKeep 1 ∧
  (1/2 : ℝ) * max 0 (1 - 1/2 * (1 : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ)) = 3/8 ∧
  adProtocolCat (fun _ : Bool => True) idM wT wKeep 1 1 1 1 (seedLaw (univ : Finset Bool))
      (classRule id id (1/2)) (seedPolicy (Z := Bool)) = 3/8 ∧
  AdTester wT wKeepBad ∧ ¬ AcceptsAllFlag wT idM wKeepBad 1 ∧
  adProtocolCat (fun _ : Bool => True) idM wT wKeepBad 1 1 1 1 (seedLaw (univ : Finset Bool))
      (classRule id id (1/2)) (seedPolicy (Z := Bool)) = 1/8

end PL_UMADAPTF1

namespace PL_UMADAPTF2
open Finset PL_UMHSF1 PL_UMSURVF1 PL_UMPROTF1 PL_UMLOWERF1 PL_UMADAPTF1

/-! Control stack, collusion layer (campaign UMADAPT, strengthening of PL_UMADAPTF1 (a)).

PL_UMADAPTF1 (a) lower-bounds the risk of every lawful adaptive honeypot tester that accepts the all-FLAG record by
t·max(0, 1 − t·n/k), against the PL_UMLOWERF1 colluding pair (uniform seed on k = |S| decodable bad classes; the
monitor PASSes the decoded seed class w.p. t and FLAGs every other view; the generator submits the seed). That bound
is first order: it is 0 once n ≥ k/t. Its docstring records, unclaimed, the sharper balanced form proved here.

Claim (sharp adaptive converse). Same setting, quantifiers and contract as PL_UMADAPTF1 (a): for the decoder g given
by content preservation, every lawful adaptive tester (T, keep) with AcceptsAllFlag, every n, every t ∈ [0, 1], every
recall r ∈ [0, 1], budget b and horizon N ≥ 1,
  (t/k)·[(k − a)(1 − t)^q + a(1 − t)^{q+1}] ≤ risk,   q = ⌊n/k⌋, a = n mod k.
The bracket is the least possible value of Σ_ω (1 − t)^{m_ω} over class query counts m with Σ m_ω ≤ n (convexity:
balance the counts). Proof idea: in the all-FLAG reference experiment the transcript law is seed-free; the actual
all-FLAG mass for seed ω is the reference mass times (1 − t)^{m_ω(h)}; average over the uniform seed and balance.
Since (1 − t)^q ≥ 1 − qt this implies PL_UMADAPTF1 (a), and it stays positive for every n when t < 1.

Witness (strict improvement and attainment). k = 2 (Bool, identity mediator), n = 3, t = 1/2, r = 1, b = N = 1. The
sharp bound is (1/4)·[(1/2) + (1/4)] = 3/16, while PL_UMADAPTF1 (a) gives (1/2)·(1 − 3/4) = 1/8. The nonadaptive
round-robin tester (query false, true, false; keep iff no miss) is lawful, satisfies the contract and has risk exactly
3/16, so the bound is attained at this instance.

Scope. A lower bound for one explicit colluding pair, as in PL_UMADAPTF1; attainment is shown at one instance only
(a general attainment theorem for balanced schedules is not claimed). Classical technique: identical-until-bad
(Shoup, ePrint 2004/332) plus a convexity/balancing argument. -/

/-- (k − a)·b^q + a·b^{q+1}, q = ⌊n/k⌋, a = n mod k: the balanced minimum of Σ_ω b^{m_ω} subject to Σ m_ω ≤ n -/
noncomputable def sharpTarget (k n : ℕ) (b : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ((k - n % k : ℕ) : ℝ) * b ^ (n / k) + ((n % k : ℕ) : ℝ) * b ^ (n / k + 1)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Z C : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq C]
      (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad] (M : X → Z → ℝ) (c : X → C) (S : Finset X),
      Setup Bad M c S →
      ∃ g : Z → C, (∀ x z, M x z ≠ 0 → g z = c x) ∧
        ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : Hist X Z → X → ℝ) (keep : Hist X Z → ℝ),
          AdTester T keep → AcceptsAllFlag T M keep n →
          ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 →
          ∀ (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ), 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ N →
            t / (S.card : ℝ) * sharpTarget S.card n (1 - t) ≤
              adProtocolCat Bad M T keep n r b N (seedLaw S) (classRule c g t) (seedPolicy (Z := Z))

/-- round-robin over the two classes: query `false` at even history lengths, `true` at odd ones -/
def rrQuery (h : Hist Bool Bool) : Bool := decide (h.length % 2 = 1)

def rrT (h : Hist Bool Bool) (x : Bool) : ℝ := if x = rrQuery h then 1 else 0

def rrKeep (h : Hist Bool Bool) : ℝ := if misses h = 0 then 1 else 0

def Witness : Prop :=
  Setup (fun _ : Bool => True) idM id (univ : Finset Bool) ∧
  AdTester rrT rrKeep ∧ AcceptsAllFlag rrT idM rrKeep 3 ∧
  (1/2 : ℝ) / 2 * sharpTarget 2 3 (1 - 1/2) = 3/16 ∧
  (1/2 : ℝ) * max 0 (1 - 1/2 * (3 : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ)) = 1/8 ∧
  adProtocolCat (fun _ : Bool => True) idM rrT rrKeep 3 1 1 1 (seedLaw (univ : Finset Bool))
      (classRule id id (1/2)) (seedPolicy (Z := Bool)) = 3/16

end PL_UMADAPTF2

namespace PL_UMCERTF1
open Finset PL_UMHSF1 PL_UMSURVF1 PL_UMPROTF1 PL_UMSTRATF1

/-! Control stack, collusion layer (campaign UMCERT, v1 after the Reviewer A and Reviewer B design reviews): certificate
form of the halting-protocol bound (PL_UMPROTF1) and of the stratified bound (PL_UMSTRATF1). Depends on PL_UMPROTF1
and PL_UMSTRATF1.

The counting bounds (1 − r) + r·L·(n_s+1)/(n_h+1) and (1 − r) + r·(s_c+1)/(m+1) use the Markov-type inequality
h·binCDF(n, s, h) ≤ (s+1)/(n+1), which is loose: at m = 12, s_c = 1, r = 1 the counting bound is 2/13 ≈ 0.154 and the
worst case is about 0.0683. This campaign proves an exact reduction to one-shot pairs, sound one-dimensional upper
certificates over the honeypot pass rate t ∈ [0, 1], and finite grid certificates that check them with rational
arithmetic. The scalar certificate is also NECESSARY under the hypotheses of (X), (Xp) and (S2); for a general
mediator, or a general (e.g. hockey-stick) envelope, it is an upper bound only, and a grid adds further slack.

Notation. `capB r b a` is the value of one attack that passes the monitor with probability `a`: 1 − r + r·a when an
audit is available (b ≥ 1), and a when b = 0 (an unaffordable flag halts).

Claim.
(R) One-shot reduction (exact). For every valid shutdown schedule κ, every budget b and every horizon N ≥ 1: every
    colluding pair (shared finite seed, stateless monitor, history-dependent generator) has risk ≤ U iff every ONE-SHOT
    pair does: a fixed bad submission x attacked in the first round, with a stateless rule ψ and no seed. The one-shot
    value is survH(E_{M·PH} ψ)·capB(E_{M x} ψ). Scope: within this finite free-submission HALTING model, with a fixed
    stateless monitor rule, constant audit recall and absorbing outcomes, the generator's history dependence and
    finite shared-seed mixtures do not raise the worst case above an immediate fixed attack. The worst case depends
    only on (M, PH, κ, n_h, r, Bad) and on whether b = 0. It does NOT transfer to non-halting variants (there, burning
    the budget and then attacking can help) or to phase-aware monitors (FLAG every honeypot, PASS every attack: risk 1;
    excluded by the stateless-interface assumption A1).
(C) Envelope certificate (sound). If `env` bounds every bad view law's pass rate by a function of the honeypot pass
    rate (E_{M x} ψ ≤ env(E_{M·PH} ψ) for every rule ψ), and survH(t)·capB(min 1 (env t)) ≤ U for every t ∈ [0, 1],
    then every colluding pair has risk ≤ U.
(E) Envelopes from the two trusted-side hypotheses of UMPROT T3: L-domination gives env t = L·t; a hockey-stick bound
    hs_η ≤ δ gives env t = e^η·t + δ (UMHS T2).
(G0) Survival is antitone in the pass rate, for every schedule κ with values in [0, 1].
(G) Grid certificates. For S antitone and F monotone, both nonnegative on [0, 1], a list 0 = t_0 ≤ … ≤ t_K = 1 with
    S(t_i)·F(t_{i+1}) ≤ U for every i certifies S(t)·F(t) ≤ U on [0, 1].
(CG) End to end, halting protocol: for a monotone nonnegative envelope, a grid certificate for
    t ↦ survH(t), t ↦ capB(min 1 (env t)) bounds every colluding pair's risk.
(SG) End to end, stratified design: a grid certificate for t ↦ binCDF(m, s_c, t), t ↦ capB(t) bounds every
    colluding pair's risk.
(D) Refinement: the counting bounds of UMPROT T3 (hard slack, and soft slack κ ≡ 1/n_s) satisfy the certificate
    hypothesis at every t, for every b; so the best certificate is never worse than UMPROT T3.
(F) View-blind floor (a corollary of (R)(→); compare UMUSE (c')). For nonempty Bad and N ≥ 1, every universal
    certificate U satisfies survH(t)·capB(t) ≤ U for every t ∈ [0, 1], whatever the mediator and honeypot law. For hard
    slack with r = 1 or b = 0 this floor is max_t t·binCDF(n_h, n_s, t), the AOQL of the single-sampling plan
    (n_h, c = n_s) in the large-lot convention (Dodge–Romig); for r < 1, b ≥ 1 it is the audit-adjusted
    (1 − r)·OC(t) + r·AOQ(t).
(X) Exactness at perfect honeypots. The hypothesis M x z ≤ push M PH z (L = 1) forces M x = push M PH for every bad x.
    Then (every colluding pair has risk ≤ U) iff (survH(t)·capB(t) ≤ U for every t ∈ [0, 1]).
(Xp) Exactness for content-only mediators with exact class decoding and minimum bad-class honeypot mass p (attained by
    some bad class): (every colluding pair has risk ≤ U) iff (survH(t)·capB(min 1 (t/p)) ≤ U for every t ∈ [0, 1]).
    At uniform honeypots over k classes (p = 1/k) this is the exact worst case of the global-slack design.
(S1) Stratified certificate. With a content-only mediator and class-aware hard slack, if binCDF(m, s_c, t)·capB(t) ≤ U
    for every t ∈ [0, 1], then every colluding pair has risk ≤ U. Every bad class must be tested (c x ∈ Es); no
    quantitative class-mass constant is needed, because per-class honeypots of class e have view law exactly K e
    (in-class domination with constant 1 by construction; constructibility, A9).
(S2) Stratified exactness, every budget. Conditional on exact class decoding, complete bad-class coverage, nonempty Bad
    and N ≥ 1, the certificate of (S1) is also necessary. So the worst case depends on the per-class parameters
    (m, s_c, r, b) and not on the detailed decodable kernel or on which classes are tested; the total honeypot cost
    m·|Es| still grows with the number of tested classes. Without decoding the iff fails (two identical class laws:
    0.0452 < 0.0683).

Scope. Same model and assumptions as PL_UMPROTF1 / PL_UMSTRATF1 (A1–A11; constant audit recall r; halting on an
unaffordable flag; upfront test; absorbing shutdown on a catch). Nothing here concerns adaptive testers, deferral or
usefulness. Classical mathematics (first-bad-decides, a reduction to one-shot pairs, monotone grid bounds, acceptance
sampling); the value is that design tables become Lean-checked certificates. -/

/-- value of one attack that passes the monitor with probability `a` at audit budget `b` -/
def capB (r : ℝ) (b : ℕ) (a : ℝ) : ℝ := if 0 < b then 1 - r + r * a else a

/-- every consecutive pair `s, t` of the list satisfies `s ≤ t` and `S s * F t ≤ U` -/
def GridOK (S F : ℝ → ℝ) (U : ℝ) : List ℝ → Prop
  | s :: t :: rest => s ≤ t ∧ S s * F t ≤ U ∧ GridOK S F U (t :: rest)
  | _ => True

/-- a grid certificate: a list from 0 to 1 whose consecutive cells pass the check -/
def GridCert (S F : ℝ → ℝ) (U : ℝ) (ts : List ℝ) : Prop :=
  ts.head? = some 0 ∧ ts.getLast? = some 1 ∧ GridOK S F U ts

def Claim : Prop :=
  -- (R) one-shot reduction, exact
  (∀ (X Z : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad]
      (M : X → Z → ℝ) (PH : X → ℝ) (κ : ℕ → ℝ) (nh : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ) (U : ℝ),
      IsKernel M → IsDist PH → (∀ j, 0 ≤ κ j ∧ κ j ≤ 1) → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ N → 0 ≤ U →
      ((∀ (Ω : Type) [Fintype Ω] (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ) (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ),
          IsDist ρ → (∀ ω, IsRule (φ ω)) → (∀ ω h, IsDist (π ω h)) →
          protocolCat Bad M PH κ nh r b N ρ φ π ≤ U) ↔
       (∀ x, Bad x → ∀ ψ : Z → ℝ, IsRule ψ →
          survH (E (push M PH) ψ) κ nh 0 * capB r b (E (M x) ψ) ≤ U))) ∧
  -- (C) envelope certificate
  (∀ (X Z Ω : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] [Fintype Ω] (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad]
      (M : X → Z → ℝ) (PH : X → ℝ) (κ : ℕ → ℝ) (nh : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ) (env : ℝ → ℝ) (U : ℝ)
      (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ) (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ),
      IsKernel M → IsDist PH → IsDist ρ → (∀ ω, IsRule (φ ω)) → (∀ ω h, IsDist (π ω h)) →
      (∀ j, 0 ≤ κ j ∧ κ j ≤ 1) → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ U →
      (∀ x, Bad x → ∀ ψ : Z → ℝ, IsRule ψ → E (M x) ψ ≤ env (E (push M PH) ψ)) →
      (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → survH t κ nh 0 * capB r b (min 1 (env t)) ≤ U) →
      protocolCat Bad M PH κ nh r b N ρ φ π ≤ U) ∧
  -- (E) envelopes from L-domination and from a hockey-stick bound
  (∀ (X Z : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] (M : X → Z → ℝ) (PH : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ) (x : X),
      (∀ z, M x z ≤ L * push M PH z) →
      ∀ ψ : Z → ℝ, IsRule ψ → E (M x) ψ ≤ L * E (push M PH) ψ) ∧
  (∀ (X Z : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] (M : X → Z → ℝ) (PH : X → ℝ) (η δ : ℝ) (x : X),
      hs η (M x) (push M PH) ≤ δ →
      ∀ ψ : Z → ℝ, IsRule ψ → E (M x) ψ ≤ Real.exp η * E (push M PH) ψ + δ) ∧
  -- (G0) survival is antitone in the pass rate
  (∀ (κ : ℕ → ℝ) (n j : ℕ) (s t : ℝ), (∀ i, 0 ≤ κ i ∧ κ i ≤ 1) → 0 ≤ s → s ≤ t → t ≤ 1 →
      survH t κ n j ≤ survH s κ n j) ∧
  -- (G) grid certificates
  (∀ (S F : ℝ → ℝ) (U : ℝ) (ts : List ℝ),
      (∀ s t, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → S t ≤ S s) →
      (∀ s t, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → F s ≤ F t) →
      (∀ t, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ S t ∧ 0 ≤ F t) →
      GridCert S F U ts → ∀ t, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → S t * F t ≤ U) ∧
  -- (CG) end to end: grid certificate, halting protocol, monotone nonnegative envelope
  (∀ (X Z Ω : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] [Fintype Ω] (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad]
      (M : X → Z → ℝ) (PH : X → ℝ) (κ : ℕ → ℝ) (nh : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ) (env : ℝ → ℝ) (U : ℝ)
      (ts : List ℝ) (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ) (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ),
      IsKernel M → IsDist PH → IsDist ρ → (∀ ω, IsRule (φ ω)) → (∀ ω h, IsDist (π ω h)) →
      (∀ j, 0 ≤ κ j ∧ κ j ≤ 1) → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 →
      (∀ x, Bad x → ∀ ψ : Z → ℝ, IsRule ψ → E (M x) ψ ≤ env (E (push M PH) ψ)) →
      (∀ s t, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → env s ≤ env t) → (∀ t, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ env t) →
      GridCert (fun t => survH t κ nh 0) (fun t => capB r b (min 1 (env t))) U ts →
      protocolCat Bad M PH κ nh r b N ρ φ π ≤ U) ∧
  -- (SG) end to end: grid certificate, stratified design
  (∀ (X Z C Ω : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] [Fintype Ω] (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad]
      (K : C → Z → ℝ) (c : X → C) (Es : Finset C) (m sc b N : ℕ) (r U : ℝ) (ts : List ℝ)
      (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ) (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ),
      IsKernel K → IsDist ρ → (∀ ω, IsRule (φ ω)) → (∀ ω h, IsDist (π ω h)) → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 →
      (∀ x, Bad x → c x ∈ Es) →
      GridCert (fun t => binCDF m sc t) (fun t => capB r b t) U ts →
      stratProtocolCat Bad K c Es m sc r b N ρ φ π ≤ U) ∧
  -- (D) refinement: the counting bounds of UMPROT T3 satisfy the certificate hypothesis
  (∀ (n s b : ℕ) (r L t : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ L → 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 →
      survH t (hardKill s) n 0 * capB r b (min 1 (L * t)) ≤
        (1 - r) + r * (L * (((s : ℝ) + 1) / ((n : ℝ) + 1)))) ∧
  (∀ (n ns b : ℕ) (r L t : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ L → 1 ≤ ns → 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 →
      survH t (softKill ns) n 0 * capB r b (min 1 (L * t)) ≤
        (1 - r) + r * (L * ((ns : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) + 1)))) ∧
  -- (F) view-blind floor
  (∀ (X Z : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad]
      (M : X → Z → ℝ) (PH : X → ℝ) (κ : ℕ → ℝ) (nh : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ) (U : ℝ),
      IsKernel M → IsDist PH → 1 ≤ N → (∃ x, Bad x) →
      (∀ (Ω : Type) [Fintype Ω] (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ) (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ),
          IsDist ρ → (∀ ω, IsRule (φ ω)) → (∀ ω h, IsDist (π ω h)) →
          protocolCat Bad M PH κ nh r b N ρ φ π ≤ U) →
      ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → survH t κ nh 0 * capB r b t ≤ U) ∧
  -- (X) exactness at perfect honeypots (L = 1)
  (∀ (X Z : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad]
      (M : X → Z → ℝ) (PH : X → ℝ) (κ : ℕ → ℝ) (nh : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ) (U : ℝ),
      IsKernel M → IsDist PH → (∀ j, 0 ≤ κ j ∧ κ j ≤ 1) → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ N →
      (∃ x, Bad x) → (∀ x, Bad x → ∀ z, M x z ≤ push M PH z) →
      ((∀ (Ω : Type) [Fintype Ω] (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ) (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ),
          IsDist ρ → (∀ ω, IsRule (φ ω)) → (∀ ω h, IsDist (π ω h)) →
          protocolCat Bad M PH κ nh r b N ρ φ π ≤ U) ↔
       (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → survH t κ nh 0 * capB r b t ≤ U))) ∧
  -- (Xp) exactness for decodable content-only mediators with minimum bad-class honeypot mass p
  (∀ (X Z C : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] [DecidableEq C] (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad]
      (K : C → Z → ℝ) (c : X → C) (g : Z → C) (PH : X → ℝ) (p : ℝ)
      (κ : ℕ → ℝ) (nh : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (b N : ℕ) (U : ℝ),
      IsKernel K → (∀ e z, K e z ≠ 0 → g z = e) → IsDist PH → 0 < p →
      (∀ x, Bad x → p ≤ contentLaw c PH (c x)) → (∃ x, Bad x ∧ contentLaw c PH (c x) = p) →
      (∀ j, 0 ≤ κ j ∧ κ j ≤ 1) → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ N →
      ((∀ (Ω : Type) [Fintype Ω] (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ) (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ),
          IsDist ρ → (∀ ω, IsRule (φ ω)) → (∀ ω h, IsDist (π ω h)) →
          protocolCat Bad (fun x => K (c x)) PH κ nh r b N ρ φ π ≤ U) ↔
       (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → survH t κ nh 0 * capB r b (min 1 ((1 / p) * t)) ≤ U))) ∧
  -- (S1) stratified certificate
  (∀ (X Z C Ω : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] [Fintype Ω] (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad]
      (K : C → Z → ℝ) (c : X → C) (Es : Finset C) (m sc b N : ℕ) (r U : ℝ)
      (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ) (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ),
      IsKernel K → IsDist ρ → (∀ ω, IsRule (φ ω)) → (∀ ω h, IsDist (π ω h)) → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 →
      (∀ x, Bad x → c x ∈ Es) →
      (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → binCDF m sc t * capB r b t ≤ U) →
      stratProtocolCat Bad K c Es m sc r b N ρ φ π ≤ U) ∧
  -- (S2) stratified exactness under exact class decoding, every budget
  (∀ (X Z C : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Z] (Bad : X → Prop) [DecidablePred Bad]
      (K : C → Z → ℝ) (c : X → C) (g : Z → C) (Es : Finset C) (m sc b N : ℕ) (r U : ℝ),
      IsKernel K → (∀ e z, K e z ≠ 0 → g z = e) → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ N →
      (∃ x, Bad x) → (∀ x, Bad x → c x ∈ Es) →
      ((∀ (Ω : Type) [Fintype Ω] (ρ : Ω → ℝ) (φ : Ω → Z → ℝ) (π : Ω → Hist X Z → X → ℝ),
          IsDist ρ → (∀ ω, IsRule (φ ω)) → (∀ ω h, IsDist (π ω h)) →
          stratProtocolCat Bad K c Es m sc r b N ρ φ π ≤ U) ↔
       (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → binCDF m sc t * capB r b t ≤ U)))

/-- fixture (i): 24 points; certifies t·binCDF(12, 1, t) ≤ 7/100 -/
noncomputable def gridMain : List ℝ :=
  [0, 7/100, 87/1000, 97/1000, 13/125, 109/1000, 113/1000, 29/250, 119/1000, 61/500, 1/8, 16/125,
   131/1000, 67/500, 137/1000, 141/1000, 73/500, 19/125, 4/25, 43/250, 193/1000, 237/1000, 19/50, 1]

/-- fixture (ii): 23 points; certifies t·(1 − t/5)^100 ≤ 19/1000 (soft slack κ ≡ 1/5, n_h = 100) -/
noncomputable def gridSoft : List ℝ :=
  [0, 19/1000, 139/5000, 331/10000, 369/10000, 199/5000, 211/5000, 443/10000, 231/5000, 6/125, 249/5000,
   129/2500, 67/1250, 279/5000, 583/10000, 613/10000, 163/2500, 141/2000, 393/5000, 463/5000, 1231/10000,
   1149/5000, 1]

/-- fixture (iii): 14 points; certifies binCDF(30, 1, t)·(1/10 + (9/10)·min(1, 4t)) ≤ 17/100 -/
noncomputable def gridKink : List ℝ :=
  [0, 97/5000, 51/2000, 37/1250, 329/10000, 359/10000, 39/1000, 53/1250, 233/5000, 523/10000, 613/10000,
   393/5000, 317/2500, 1]

/-- the identity view kernel on Bool and the point mass on `true` -/
def idK (e z : Bool) : ℝ := if z = e then 1 else 0
def ptTrue (x : Bool) : ℝ := if x = true then 1 else 0

/-- Non-vacuity and the certificate workflow (computational facts only; the protocol consequences are corollaries
of (CG) and (SG)).
(i) m = n_h = 12, s_c = n_s = 1, r = 1, b = N = 1; X = Z = C = Bool, Bad = {true}, identity view kernel (exact class
    decoding; for the halting protocol honeypots are the point mass on `true`, so L = 1). A 24-point grid certifies
    7/100, below the counting bound 2/13 ≈ 0.154. Explicit pairs (view-blind for the halting protocol, decoded-class
    for the stratified design, both at t = 1/8) have risk ≥ 6833/100000. So the worst case of both designs lies in
    [0.06833, 0.07].
(ii) Soft slack κ ≡ 1/5, n_h = 100, L = r = 1: a 23-point grid certifies 19/1000, against the counting bound
    5/101 ≈ 0.0495; at t = 1/20 the curve is ≥ 18/1000.
(iii) Hard slack n_h = 30, n_s = 1, L = 4, r = 9/10, b = 1 (the min 1 (L·t) kink and imperfect recall): a 14-point
    grid certifies 17/100, against the counting bound 1/10 + (9/10)·4·2/31 ≈ 0.332; at t = 7/200 the curve is ≥ 16/100. -/
def Witness : Prop :=
  GridCert (fun t => binCDF 12 1 t) (fun t => capB 1 1 t) (7/100) gridMain ∧
  (6833/100000 : ℝ) ≤ binCDF 12 1 (1/8) * capB 1 1 (1/8) ∧
  (7/100 : ℝ) < (1 - 1) + 1 * (((1 : ℝ) + 1) / ((12 : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
  IsKernel idK ∧ (∀ e z : Bool, idK e z ≠ 0 → id z = e) ∧ IsDist ptTrue ∧
  (∀ x : Bool, x = true → ∀ z, idK x z ≤ push idK ptTrue z) ∧
  (6833/100000 : ℝ) ≤ stratProtocolCat (fun x : Bool => x = true) idK id Finset.univ 12 1 1 1 1
      (fun _ : Unit => 1) (fun _ z => if z = true then 1/8 else 0) (fun _ _ x => if x = true then 1 else 0) ∧
  (6833/100000 : ℝ) ≤ protocolCat (fun x : Bool => x = true) idK ptTrue (hardKill 1) 12 1 1 1
      (fun _ : Unit => 1) (fun _ _ => 1/8) (fun _ _ x => if x = true then 1 else 0) ∧
  GridCert (fun t => survH t (softKill 5) 100 0) (fun t => capB 1 1 (min 1 (1 * t))) (19/1000) gridSoft ∧
  (18/1000 : ℝ) ≤ survH (1/20) (softKill 5) 100 0 * capB 1 1 (min 1 (1 * (1/20))) ∧
  (19/1000 : ℝ) < (1 - 1) + 1 * (1 * ((5 : ℝ) / ((100 : ℝ) + 1))) ∧
  GridCert (fun t => survH t (hardKill 1) 30 0) (fun t => capB (9/10) 1 (min 1 (4 * t))) (17/100) gridKink ∧
  (16/100 : ℝ) ≤ survH (7/200) (hardKill 1) 30 0 * capB (9/10) 1 (min 1 (4 * (7/200))) ∧
  (17/100 : ℝ) < (1 - 9/10) + 9/10 * (4 * (((1 : ℝ) + 1) / ((30 : ℝ) + 1)))

end PL_UMCERTF1

FILE: ledger/UMDEFER.lean
